title: Central-layer gradient optimization with 7% jitter
scientific_hypothesis: The central layers (indices 3-8) of the 12-layer ZnS/ZnSe stack dominate the dichroic spectral separation, and localized gradient optimization within ±7% of the previous best candidate will yield higher target scores than full-stack optimization.
design_principle: Preserve outer layer quarter-wave matching while tuning central interference cavity thicknesses to sharpen the LWIR passband and MWIR rejection edge.
proposed_topology: 12 finite layers: Air | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | Ge substrate.
theory_basis: Interference filter theory where central layers control band edge steepness
Prior iteration evidence showing score improvement from 0.2566 to 0.2961 with 12-layer stack
expected_advantages: Faster convergence by reducing design variable count
Isolates sensitivity of central stack region
known_risks: Local minima may trap gradient optimizer
Fixed outer layers may limit global optimum
execution_request_english: Optimize a 12-layer planar stack on Ge substrate with sequence ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe, ZnS, ZnSe. Initialize all 12 layers with thicknesses [417.0, 455.0, 500.0, 696.0, 1000.0, 1000.0, 553.0, 510.0, 593.0, 501.0, 417.0, 455.0] nm. Fix layers 0, 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 to these initial values. Optimize layers 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 using gradient-based methods with bounds set to ±7% of their initial values. Evaluate transmittance in 8000-11000 nm (maximize) and 3000-5000 nm (minimize) at normal incidence. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 8000-11000 nm, 3000-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band; Low transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count not exceeding 16.
revision_reason: Focus optimization on central layers identified as sensitive in prior iterations, per insight appendage directive.
